value.overview: The Elegant Euphonia is a small, colorful finch of mountainous Central America and Mexico. It is also called the Blue-hooded Euphonia because adult males have a striking turquoise-blue hood. The species usually occurs in pairs or small groups and is closely associated with mistletoe-bearing trees, whose berries form much of its diet. In Costa Rica it is a fairly uncommon highland bird, especially associated with mountain forests and nearby wooded edges.
value.classification: The Elegant Euphonia belongs to the finch family Fringillidae and the genus Chlorophonia. The Costa Rican population is generally treated as the subspecies Chlorophonia elegantissima vincens.
value.identification: This small euphonia has a short, stout bill and a compact body. The adult male has a bright turquoise-blue crown and hood, a dark throat, greenish upperparts, and rich rusty or chestnut underparts, often with a contrasting reddish forehead. The female is more subdued, mainly greenish, with a blue hood and rusty tones on the forehead. Its rapid, liquid song may include warbles, chatters, buzzes, and clear whistles.
value.rangeHabitat: The Elegant Euphonia ranges from Mexico through parts of Central America to western Panama. In Costa Rica, it occurs mainly in the mountainous interior, including the Cordillera de Tilarán and other highland areas, generally from about 1,200 to 2,500 meters. It uses humid montane evergreen forest, pine-oak woodland, secondary forest, wooded edges, farmland hedgerows, and brushy habitats. Mistletoe-bearing trees are especially important, and the species may visit gardens or semi-open areas near suitable highland forest.
value.migrationStatus: It is generally resident in Costa Rica, but post-breeding movements to lower elevations are documented. These local altitudinal movements can make it appear seasonal in some areas; it is not a regular long-distance migrant there.
value.breeding: The breeding season is not fully defined, and detailed information from Costa Rica is limited. The nest is a globular structure with a side entrance, woven from dry grass, rootlets, and other plant fibers. It may be placed in a niche in an earthen bank, among moss or epiphytes, or on a tree trunk or branch fork, sometimes well above the ground. Reported clutches contain about three whitish eggs marked with reddish-brown spots.
value.dietFeeding: The Elegant Euphonia feeds mainly on small soft berries, especially fruits of mistletoes in the family Loranthaceae. It often searches through fruiting trees in pairs or small groups, sometimes forming larger wandering flocks when food is abundant. Birds may remove the outer covering of mistletoe berries before swallowing the pulp and seeds. Its dependence on fruiting mistletoe helps explain its close association with mature, wooded habitats.
value.behavior: This active but sometimes inconspicuous bird usually forages in pairs or small groups within dense foliage. It often remains near mistletoe clumps and may sing persistently from concealed perches. Groups can move widely between fruiting trees, and local movements may include descending to lower elevations after breeding. The species has a rapid, varied song and sharp call notes. It may gather communally to roost in dense vegetation.

conservation.populationTrend: The global population is considered to be decreasing, although the species remains fairly common across much of its broad range. In Costa Rica it is generally described as fairly uncommon.
